founder.heading: About Dr. Jean-Clément Diambilay
founder.p1: Dr. Jean-Clément Diambilay is a Congolese economist and entrepreneur, and the founder of the Diambilay Business Center.
founder.p2: His path begins in Lubumbashi, where he earned a licence in Economic Sciences from the University of Lubumbashi in 1999. After certifying in international taxation and VAT in Norway, he spent three years (2010–2013) in the tax department of DNB Bank ASA, Norway's largest financial services group.
founder.p3: Back in central Africa he founded Goodwin Trading Investments, J.C. Consulting, Neema Consulting Mining and Adon Technology — a portfolio spanning commerce and finance, strategic consulting, mining and digital.
founder.p4: In 2023 he founded the Diambilay Business Center at 378 Avenue Likasi in Lubumbashi to take African entrepreneurs from idea to investable business. DBC was admitted to AfriLabs — the largest African network of innovation hubs — on 6 September 2024, and has since grown into a multi-country structure across DR Congo, France, South Africa and Germany. He convened the first Forum Richesses d'Afrique at the Palais des Sports Robert Charpentier in Issy-les-Moulineaux on 17 May 2025, with former French minister Élisabeth Moreno as godmother of the event; a second edition followed in Montréal on 22 November. He has authored more than thirty books on entrepreneurship, leadership and personal development.

intros.news: The DBC Germany journal covers the African-rooted business community in Europe — founder stories, policy briefs, capital updates, and long-form pieces on the companies shaping the diaspora economy. Expect notes from the ground in Düsseldorf, Berlin, Paris, and Lubumbashi, alongside reporting on Richesses d'Afrique Germany 2026 and our programmes. We publish in three languages; German and French versions usually follow the English one within a few days. Subscribe to the newsletter on /newsletter to get one curated brief per week — the archive lives below.
intros.team: Meet the operators behind DBC Germany. The Düsseldorf office runs incubation, investment prep, courses, mentorship, and the annual Richesses d'Afrique conference. The names below are the people you'll actually work with if you apply to a programme, pitch a partnership, or come to an event. Each profile links to the person's professional background and the programmes they lead. If you don't see the role you need, contact us — we hire for operator-grade generalists more often than titles suggest.
intros.contact: Reach DBC Germany via whichever channel matches your query. Press and media enquiries go to the press desk; we respond within 24 hours on weekdays. Incubation and programme applications live on /services/incubation/apply and land directly in our review queue. Partnership and sponsorship conversations — including Richesses d'Afrique Germany 2026 packages — go through the form below or to jay@dbc-germany.com. For everything else (general questions, speaker suggestions, non-urgent media queries) the form below reaches the right person the same day.

items.q: Do I need a finished idea to apply?
items.a: No. If you don't have an idea yet, we'll skip the idea questions and help you find one through our courses and mentorship network.

items.q: Which languages can I apply in?
items.a: English, German, or French. The office responds in your language within 10 business days.

items.q: Is this only for founders in Germany?
items.a: No. DBC Germany — the DACH branch — welcomes applicants from the wider African diaspora across Europe and beyond.

items.q: Is there a cost to apply?
items.a: The application is free. Fees only apply to specific paid programs (courses, masterclasses, events) once you are matched to one.
